transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I feel like God’s picked me out personally to fix everything in this town, and nobody understands how important my mission is. My wife and the people at work are acting like I'm doing something wrong, but I'm just trying to do what I've been chosen to do.
During this time, have you also felt unusually energetic or needed much less sleep than usual? Have you been talking more than usual or feeling like your thoughts are racing?

Yes, absolutely! I feel completely revved up and only need three or four hours of sleep a night without ever feeling tired. My mind races so fast with plans to fix the agency and start new ministries that I talk a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to the next before my wife can even keep up.

Before this current episode, have you ever had another period lasting several days or longer when you felt similarly high, energized, needed little sleep, or had unusual beliefs? Or have you ever had a major depressive episode with at least two weeks of feeling very down or losing interest in things?
I don't recall ever having times like this before everything started about a year and a half ago. I'm also not really sure if I've ever had a major depressive episode where I felt down like that.

Before this started a year and a half ago, did you ever have a period of at least several days when you felt unusually depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in almost everything? Or was this current high-energy, grand mission state the first major mood episode you’ve ever had?

I don't really remember having any periods of feeling depressed or hopeless before all of this started a year and a half ago. This high-energy mission I'm on right now is really the first and main thing I've ever had to deal with.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first major mood episode characterized by elevated/expansive mood with grandiose religious delusions, markedly decreased need for sleep, pressured/increased speech, racing thoughts, and increased goal-directed activity. Psychotic symptoms are present in the context of a manic syndrome, and there is no history provided of prior depressive episodes or earlier similar episodes. This is most consistent with a manic episode with psychotic symptoms.
